explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/386: for 2 ≤ k ≤ n-2, can C(n,k) be a product of consecutive primes infinitely often (e.g. C(21,2) = 2·3·5·7)? Open. The statement asserts that infinitely many n admit some k with 2 ≤ k ≤ n-2 and C(n,k) = ∏_{i∈[p,q)} p_i. Empty or one-prime products cannot occur in this range, since C(n,k) is neither 1 nor prime there. Faithful.
